title: EV Powertrain Engineer
summary: EV powertrain engineers make the traction motor, inverter and battery pack work together in an electric vehicle and prove it through bench, dyno and road tests. They sit in a vehicle engineering team at an EV maker or supplier, between the component teams and the vehicle launch team.
dailyDuties: Plan powertrain tests and keep the DVP&R up to date
Run motor dyno, chassis dyno and on-road tests
Analyse logged CAN and test data for torque, efficiency and heat
Calibrate torque maps and regen settings during vehicle trials
Debug inverter, motor and controller faults with suppliers
Estimate range and energy use for new vehicle variants
Report test results and open issues to the programme team

skills.expectation: Understand how the traction motor, inverter, battery pack and vehicle controller work together
Integrate powertrain parts on the vehicle and own the DVP&R and sign-off tests
Plan and run motor dyno, chassis dyno and on-road tests and analyse logged data
Check traction motor torque, efficiency and thermal limits against vehicle needs
Work with inverter and DC-DC suppliers on ratings, derating and faults
Calibrate torque maps, regen and drive modes with INCA or CANape
Debug CAN traffic and fault codes with CANoe or CANalyzer
Analyse test data and build powertrain models in MATLAB and Simulink
Estimate range, gradeability and energy use to size the powertrain
Understand cell behaviour, pack limits and thermal effects on range
Lead DFMEA for powertrain mounting and high-voltage integration
Close field and test failures with 8D or fishbone analysis
Follow ISO 26262 work products for powertrain functions
Use HIL benches to test powertrain controllers before vehicle trials
Automate test data processing and reports
Coordinate motor, inverter and battery suppliers and in-house teams

certifications.why: ISO 26262 depth for safety-relevant powertrain functions
